TP0136.info:
TP0136 is a surface-exposed lipoprotein of _T. pallidum_ that plays a critical role in adhesion and pathogenesis.
It facilitates the binding of bacteria to host endothelial cells and the extracellular matrix.
TP0136 has been the focus of extensive research as a potential primary syphilis vaccine candidate, given its surface exposure [DOI s41541-025-01330-7](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41541-025-01330-7).
TP0136 is employed to characterize and differentiate _T. pallidum_ subspecies, particularly subsp. _pertenue_, the agent of yaws [PMC 6197692](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6197692/).

Additional information on TP0136 can be found at:
- [UniProt O83172](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/O83172/entry)

TP0326.info:
TP0326 (BamA) is the central component of the molecular machinery that inserts OMPs into the spirochete's outer membrane.
TP0326 is bipartite and consists of a predicted 16-stranded β-barrel with eight extracellular loops (ECLs) and five polypeptide transport-associated (POTRA) domains within the periplasm.
It has been demonstrated that pools of human syphilitic sera from the USA and Colombia exhibited the capacity to recognize both the N-terminal POTRA-containing and C-terminal beta-barrel domains, as well as ECL4.
This finding suggests that TP0326 stimulates the human immune system and might constitute a potential vaccine target [PMC 4420902](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4420902/).

Additional information on TP0326 can be found at:
- [UniProt O83346](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/O83346/entry)

TP0435.info:
TP0435 (also Tp17/Tpp17) is a highly abundant lipoprotein found in _T. pallidum_ that is partially exposed on the surface of the bacterium.
While the precise function of this protein is not yet fully elucidated, research findings indicate its role as a cytadhesin, facilitating the binding of the bacterium to mammalian cells.
TP0435 has been identified as an immunodominant antigen [DOI srep25593](https://www.nature.com/articles/srep25593).

Additional information on TP0435 can be found at:
- [UniProt P29722](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P29722/entry)

TP0548.info:
TP0548 belongs to the FadL family, which facilitates the transport of long-chain fatty acids across the outer membrane, thereby providing essential nutrients for the bacterium.
Its encoding gene is of particular importance in the context of various typing approaches [PMID 33093286](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33093286/).

Additional information on TP0548 can be found at:
- [UniProt O83559](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/O83559/entry)

TP0574.info:
TP0574 (also Tp47/Tpp47) is a penicillin-binding outer membrane lipoprotein.
It has been demonstrated that TP0574-induced PGE2 production contributes to the inhibition of macrophage phagocytosis, which potentially facilitates immune evasion during infection [PMID 38258964](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38258964/).

Additional information on TP0574 can be found at:
- [UniProt P29723](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P29723/entry)

TP0705.info:
TP0705 is a periplasmic penicillin-binding protein, which is essential for the synthesis and cross-linking of the bacterial cell wall.
Recent studies have identified specific genetic variations, notably the A1873G mutation, that are associated with reduced susceptibility to penicillin G and ceftriaxone in _T. pallidum_ [PMC 12152143](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12152143/).

Additional information on TP0705 can be found at:
- [UniProt O83703 ](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprot/O83703/entry)

TP0751.info:
Pallilysin, a multifunctional metalloprotease and vascular adhesin, facilitates the dissemination of _T. pallidum_ throughout its host by employing its lipocalin domain to firmly attach the bacteria to host cells and components of the extracellular matrix [DOI s41598-017-01589-4](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-017-01589-4).

Additional information on TP0751 can be found at:
- [UniProt O83732](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/O83732/entry)

meta.description: **Syphilis** is a resurging global health threat caused by _Treponema pallidum_ ssp. _pallidum_, with additional disease burden from the closely related subspecies _pertenue_ and _endemicum_, the causative agents of yaws and bejel, respectively. By 2026 whole genome sequencing data for more than 3,000 _T. pallidum_ strains were available in the NCBI Sequence Read Archive. However, more than 80% of these lack publicly available genome assemblies and, more critically, systematic annotation. This severely limits their utility for molecular epidemiology, resistance surveillance, and vaccine development. **We aim at democratizing access to _T. pallidum_ genomic diversity data by developing and maintaining unified, community-facing Nextstrain datasets for epidemiological surveillance, comparative evolutionary analysis and facilitated data sharing; with a special emphasis on tracking outer membrane protein (OMP) diversity relevant for vaccine design.** ##### Features In addition to [Nextstrain's standard features](https://docs.nextstrain.org/en/latest/learn/interpret/index.html), this customized Auspice implementation enables a **more comprehensive investigation of protein diversity**. The Nucleotide diversity of genome panel is annotated with selected genes. Clicking on one of these genes, or selecting it using the controls in the sidebar, switches the view to show the Amino acid diversity of that gene. This view offers curated annotations of protein features, specifically the topology of outer membrane proteins. This provides a deeper insight into, for example, the diversity of extracellular loops (ECLs), which are a key target for vaccine design. In addition, an information panel is displayed below that provides more details on the protein, including links to external resources. We are working diligently to provide access to more data modalities, such as gene expression, sequence data, and more comprehensive sample annotations regarding upcoming classification schemas and the latest MLSTs. ##### Dataset The TPA-SS14 dataset currently comprises whole-genome variants of 2,487 individual _Treponema pallidum_ ssp. _pallidum_, _pertenue_, and _endemicum_ samples, genotyped against the SS14 reference genome [NC_021508.1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/nuccore/NC_021508.1/). Variants include **single nucleotide variants (SNVs) and InDels**, providing insight into the full spectrum of sequence changes and featuring the complete phylogenetic context of _T. pallidum_. **Note:** Given that the reported genotyping is based on an SS14 reference genome, reported variants may be reference-biased. Consequently, indel calls, particularly in homopolymeric regions, should be interpreted with caution. This extends to gene sequences inferred from the reported variants. ##### Metadata Accompanying **metadata includes** the sampling Date, Country, and Region, as well as Subspecies designations, including division into the Nichols and SS14 lineages. Moreover, the **sublineage and Bayesian analysis of population structure (BAP) assignments** introduced by [Beale _et al._ 2021](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41564-021-01000-z), [Taouk _et al._ 2022](https://doi.org/10.1016/s2666-5247(22)00035-0), and [Sena _et al._ 2024](https://doi.org/10.1016/S2666-5247(24)00087-9) are available. To communicate **data quality**, we provide the Effective Coverage as the mean coverage multiplied by the breadth of coverage (≥5X) per sample. Available whole genome sequencing samples with a breadth of coverage below 75% at 5X were excluded from the dataset. To raise awareness of **antimicrobial resistance (AMR)**, we annotate known resistance-associated variants: - **Macrolide resistance** mediated by 23S rRNA mutations A2058G (positions 283,691 and 235,246 in the used reference genome) and A2059G (positions 283,692 and 235,247 in the used reference genome) [PMC 3592075](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3592075/). - Putative **ceftriaxone and penicillin G resistance** associated with TP0705 variants of interest (VOIs) A1873G (position 773,095 in the used reference genome) and G2122A (position 772,846 in the used reference genome) [PMC 12152143](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12152143/). --- ##### Funding and Data Provenance This project receives funding [To support the development of a broadly effective syphilis vaccine (INV-072205)](https://www.gatesfoundation.org/about/committed-grants/2024/12/inv-072205) by the _Gates Foundation_. We gratefully acknowledge the authors, originating and submitting laboratories of the genetic sequences and metadata for sharing their work. Data producers should be named where possible and cooperation should be sought in certain circumstances. Please avoid scooping the work of others and reach out if uncertain. By clicking on a leaf node, the user can access detailed author information, raw data, and genome sequences (if available) via the linked NCBI accessors in the tooltips. ##### Medical Disclaimer The inclusion of medical and genetic information in this project is intended solely for research, educational, and informational purposes. It is not intended to be used as a substitute for professional medical advice, diagnosis, treatment, or care.
